items.title: Positive Breakout: These 6 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty 500 pack, six stocks gained over 4% and their closing prices crossed above their respective 200-day moving averages (DMA) on November 8, 2026, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. The 200-day moving average (DMA) is used by traders as a key indicator for determining the overall trend of a stock. As long as a stock's price remains above its 200-day moving average on the daily timeframe, it is generally interpreted as being in an overall uptrend.

items.title: Under attack, banks bolster cyber covers, opt for higher sum assured to protect against hits
items.description: For large financial institutions, the biggest impact often is the loss arising from systems remaining unavailable after an attack, rather than the immediate cost of the breach. Besides business interruption, ransomware, data theft, cyber extortion and third-party liabilities are among the key risks.

items.title: M&M bets on SUV growth, EV expansion and global aerospace orders to drive earnings
items.description: Mahindra & Mahindra has unveiled impressive revenue and profit figures, driven largely by the rising popularity of SUVs and electric vehicles. Looking ahead, the company is set to boost production capacity and launch several new vehicles. In contrast, the tractor sector's growth forecast has been adjusted to flat, influenced by unfavorable monsoon conditions and low water levels in reservoirs.

items.title: Agri loans emerge as biggest asset quality risk for Indian banks
items.description: Agricultural loans in India are currently facing significant asset-quality risks, with bad-loan ratios surpassing other sectors. The gross non-performing asset ratio for agricultural loans is at 5.1%, compared to 1.5% for industry and services. Factors such as a poor monsoon have contributed to this situation, although agricultural bad loans have declined since 2020-21. Various banks have reported increased agricultural loan slippages but maintain a cautious outlook on borrower stress.

items.title: Sensex & Nifty fall in Muhurat trade for first time since 2017
items.description: Indian equities experienced a slight decline during the Diwali Muhurat trading session for the first time since 2017. The Sensex ended at 80,999.40, down 28.62 points, and the Nifty closed at 24,986.40, shedding 43.95 points. Despite the drop, market sentiment has recently shown signs of improvement, particularly with foreign investors becoming buyers again.

items.title: NBFCs eye rate hikes, higher fees to offset insurance income hit
items.description: Non-bank lenders and housing finance companies are expected to raise lending rates in response to proposed regulatory changes. This adjustment aims to offset potential income losses from caps on insurance distribution. Companies such as Bajaj Housing Finance and Home First Finance are considering changing their product mix and increasing fees. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India has proposed stringent commission cuts on credit-linked insurance products.

items.title: D-Street poised for positive start as GIFT Nifty signals gains
items.description: The Indian market concluded lower during the special Muhurat Trading session, breaking a seven-session winning streak. Analysts indicate strong institutional participation and corporate earnings underpin the market structure. India VIX rose by 12% to reflect increased market fear, settling at 17.46 levels. Foreign portfolio investors net bought shares worth Rs 13,749 crore, while domestic investors sold shares.

items.title: Stocks in news: M&M, BHEL, Adani Enterprises, Wipro, Tata Steel, Siemens and Divi's Labs
items.description: Indian equity markets ended marginally lower on Sunday, breaking a seven-session winning streak. The NSE Nifty 50 decreased by 44 points, closing at 24,986. Several companies, including Adani Enterprises and Tata Steel, announced important corporate developments and new investments. Wipro appointed a new CEO for its Americas unit, while various firms reported their quarterly earnings. Overall, investors remain cautious as they monitor these announcements and future market movements.

items.title: Analysts see Nifty climbing to 25,600, recommend buying on dips
items.description: Nifty gained over 8.5% last week, crossing the 25,000 mark and demonstrating bullish momentum. Analysts foresee further upside towards 25,300-25,600 despite possible consolidation due to volatility. Key support for the Nifty is located at 24,000, promoting buying on potential dips. Top stocks recommended include Adani Ports, MCX, and SBI, showing strong bullish signals. Market breadth improved, with over half of Nifty 50 stocks above their 200-day moving averages.

items.title: Stock Radar: Infosys stocks showing signs of bottoming out after falling over 30% from highs; time to buy?
items.description: Infosys Ltd has established a support base around the 1,000 level, indicating potential recovery. Technical analysis suggests that the stock could rise to 1,400 levels in the coming months. The daily Relative Strength Index shows bullish indicators suggesting recovering momentum. Investors are advised to accumulate shares in the 1,140 to 1,190 range while maintaining a closing stop loss below 980. This consolidation phase signals possible future gains for long-term investors.

items.title: IREDA stock rises 8%, logs seventh straight session of gains; rebounds over 21% from October low
items.description: IREDA shares extended their winning streak to a seventh consecutive session on Monday, rising as much as 8% on the NSE. The stock has rebounded over 21% from its October low of Rs 98.78. The rally comes after the company's Q2 results and a recent board-level change.

items.title: HSBC upgrades India, downgrades China. Here are the sectors it likes now
items.description: HSBC has upgraded Indian equities to overweight and downgraded mainland China to neutral, citing improved valuations, stronger credit growth and resilient corporate earnings. The global brokerage favours financials, autos, industrials and consumer discretionary stocks, while remaining cautious on IT, staples and oil and gas amid growth and margin concerns.

items.title: NSE rolls out direct-to-chip liquid cooling to scale AI computing capabilities; plans to scale GPU capacity beyond 80 this quarter
items.description: The NSE has deployed Direct-to-Chip Liquid Cooling technology at its on-premises data centre to support expanding AI infrastructure. The exchange plans to scale its GPU capacity to more than 80 units this quarter, with the cooling system designed to accommodate up to 224 GPUs across high-density racks.

items.title: Stock Market Holiday 2026: Is stock market closed on Tuesday? Check remaining holidays for the year
items.description: The BSE and NSE will remain closed on November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada, while MCX will suspend trading during the morning session and reopen in the evening. The holiday follows a weak Muhurat Trading session, in which the Sensex and Nifty ended lower for the first time in nine years.

items.title: Nithin Kamath says speculative craziness brought more people into US markets: ‘Nothing expands markets like greed, FOMO
items.description: Zerodha CEO Nithin Kamath highlighted the rapid transformation of US financial markets since COVID-19, driven by crypto, derivatives, NFTs and prediction markets. While speculative trading attracts new investors and expands financial participation, Kamath warned that easy access to high-risk investments could harm individuals and society.

items.title: Stock Picks of the Week: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 35% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: The market weathered a whole bad patch with almost no FPI money coming in. But it cuts the other way too. When so little has been flowing in, even a small amount of FPI buying can move the market more than it normally would. That said, the mood has turned from bearish to cautiously optimistic, thanks largely to dropping oil prices. None of that changes your basic job as an investor: Study companies, look at earnings, and keep quality front and centre.

items.title: Explained: Why Nvidia shares dropped 4% in overnight trade and what analysts warn can trigger a bloodbath?
items.description: Nvidia shares dropped over 4% after CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang. Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice, a Chinese national, raised security concerns following intelligence reports. Nvidia has initiated an investigation into these allegations, although the board believes no secrets were compromised. Analysts suggest the company's upcoming earnings report will be crucial for market sentiment. Concerns linger over Huang's position if further evidence of wrongdoing emerges.

items.title: HSBC, Citi turn bullish as Indian stocks draw record inflows
items.description: Global banks are turning more positive on Indian stocks, indicating potential for continued growth and record foreign inflows. Recent data shows that India’s benchmark index surged nearly 8% this month, marking its best performance since mid-2022. As foreign investors shift back to Indian equities, analysts expect significant inflows and improved earnings growth in the coming fiscal years. Falling oil prices are also projected to support corporate profits and economic stability.

items.title: Nuvama Wealth Management Q2 Results: Profit rises 19% YoY to Rs 304 crore
items.description: Nuvama Wealth Management Ltd achieved a consolidated net profit of Rs 303.5 crore for Q2 FY27. The company saw a revenue increase of 20.35% to Rs 1,366 crore for the same quarter. Client assets reached Rs 5.5 lakh crore, reflecting a 25% year-on-year growth. Wealth management, asset services, and capital markets drove this substantial growth. The company demonstrated strong operating profits with a return on equity remaining robust at 29%.

items.title: Samvat 2083 stock picks: 10 ideas from India’s top brokerages for the next Diwali
items.description: Brokerages have identified 10 stocks across banking, defence, hospitality, quick commerce, consumption and manufacturing for Samvat 2083. Kotak Mahindra Bank, Bharat Electronics, Indian Hotels, Adani Ports and Eternal feature among their picks, backed by earnings visibility, strong balance sheets and structural growth opportunities. Their target prices suggest further upside potential.

items.title: Honasa Consumer shares climb 5% as Jefferies raises target price after Q2 show. Why is the brokerage bullish?
items.description: Honasa Consumer, the firm behind Mamaearth, saw a remarkable boost in its shares after revealing impressive quarterly earnings. The company recorded a nearly 87% increase in consolidated net profit for the September quarter compared to the same period last year. This surge in revenues marked the greatest growth since Honasa’s market debut. Jefferies has also upgraded its target price for the company, citing strong performance and promising future profitability.

items.title: Gland Pharma shares jump 4% after Q2 profit jumps 58%, revenue rises 23% YoY
items.description: Gland Pharma shares rose 3.89% after reporting strong Q2 FY27 results, with revenue growing 23% and net profit jumping 58% year-on-year. The stock touched a 52-week high of Rs 3,345, supported by robust CDMO growth, improved margins, new product launches and increased US regulatory approvals.

items.title: Stock market holiday this week: BSE, NSE opened on Sunday but will be closed on this day
items.description: BSE and NSE will remain closed on November 10 for Diwali-Balipratipada, while MCX will operate only during the evening session. Markets will reopen after the holiday, with November 24 and December 25 marking the remaining stock market holidays in 2026.

items.title: Sai Life Sciences shares jump 9%, multibagger stock rallies 19% in 3 days after Q2 results. Why Jefferies hiked target price
items.description: Sai Life Sciences shares hit a fresh 52-week high on Monday after strong Q2 results and bullish brokerage commentary. Jefferies retained its Buy rating and raised its target price to Rs 2,050, citing healthy CRO and CDMO growth, a strengthening pipeline and improved earnings prospects.

items.title: Divi’s Laboratories shares gain another 5% after Q2 results. Here’s why Jefferies raised target price by 23%
items.description: Shares of Divi’s Laboratories jumped 5% following a 64% YoY surge in Q2 FY27 net profit to Rs 1,127 crore. Brokerage Jefferies raised its target price by 23% to Rs 12,550, citing robust CDMO business expansion, strong EBITDA margins, and a solid GLP peptide pipeline.

items.title: Vedant Poly Fabs shares to list on SME platform today; check GMP ahead of debut
items.description: Shares of Vedant Poly Fabs will list on the NSE SME platform today, November 9. The Rs 56.68 crore IPO saw 1.90 times overall subscription. Grey market premium indicates a marginal listing gain around Rs 95 per share against the issue price of Rs 94.
